Aucun corrigé officiel ; les corrigés sont des réponses modèles de manuel de logique traditionnelle (définitions, règles de distribution, carré des oppositions avec import existentiel, ordres de l'enthymème : 1er = majeure supprimée, 2e = mineure supprimée, 3e = conclusion supprimée). Les tables de vérité, la validité des syllogismes (AOO-2, EOO-1, EIO-4) et du dilemme sont recalculées avec Python. À faire relire par un enseignant de logique : les définitions varient d'un manuel à l'autre.

Règle de choix : la page de garde dit « Answer FIVE questions, taking ALL the THREE Questions from Section A and ANY TWO from Section B ; only the first five questions answered will be marked ». Section A (questions 1 à 3) : toutes obligatoires, donc aucune règle ; Section B (questions 4 à 6) : `parmi 2 sur 3`. La règle « les cinq premières réponses seules sont corrigées » est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.
Points : chaque question est imprimée « 20 marks » ; chaque sous-question (a) à (e) vaut 4 points (« 2 x 2 marks », sauf Q2(a) imprimée « 4 x 1 marks »). 5 x 4 = 20 : aucun écart de somme.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) State:

(i) The rules of Obversion.

(ii) The terms found in the Major Premise of a Categorical Syllogism. (2 x 2 marks)

(d) (i) When is a Hypothetical Syllogism considered to be Pure?

(ii) What makes Formal Fallacies different from Informal Fallacies? (2 x 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** A hypothetical syllogism is **pure** when **all three propositions** (major premise, minor premise and conclusion) are **hypothetical** (conditional). Form: If A then B; if B then C; therefore if A then C. Example: "If it rains, the road is wet; if the road is wet, driving is dangerous; therefore if it rains, driving is dangerous." (It is **mixed** when the major premise is hypothetical but the minor premise and the conclusion are categorical.)

**(ii)** A **formal fallacy** is an error in the **structure (form)** of the argument: a rule of valid reasoning is broken, so the fault can be seen whatever the content is (e.g. undistributed middle, affirming the consequent). An **informal fallacy** is an error that comes from the **content**, the meaning or the language of the argument (ambiguity, irrelevance, unwarranted assumptions: e.g. appeal to force, begging the question, hasty generalisation), not from its form; it can only be found by examining what is said.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(e) Briefly explain the following concepts:

(i) A variable.

(ii) Logical connective. (2 x 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** A **variable** is a letter or symbol (such as $p$, $q$, $r$) that stands for any statement of a given kind and not for one particular statement; it can take either of the two truth-values, true or false. Example: in $p \supset q$, $p$ and $q$ stand for any two statements.

**(ii)** A **logical connective** is a word or symbol used to join statements into a compound statement (or to modify one), so that the truth-value of the compound depends only on the truth-values of its components. Examples: $\cdot$ (and: conjunction), $\vee$ (or: disjunction), $\supset$ (if ... then: implication), $\equiv$ (if and only if: equivalence), $\sim$ (not: negation).
themes: O Level Logic - symbolic logic basics
